title.narrative: Provision of essential Primary Health Care Services to the conflict-affected population Al Hasakeh, Northeast Syria

description.narrative: ltpgtThis project aims to address urgent health needs and reduce morbidity and mortality in Al-Hasakeh Governorate, NES, by improving access to quality, comprehensive, and inclusive primary health care services including nutrition, sexual and reproductive health (SRH), mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS) and epidemic response for conflict-affected populations in Tel Hamis, Tel Brak, and Gharra. The intervention consists of four core components:A) Continuity of PHC consultations including MHPSS, SRH, nutrition, and epidemic prevention B) Capacity strengthening through ongoing training and supervision of medical staff and community health workers (CHWs) C) Community health outreach to promote well-being, health education, and disease prevention D) Emergency preparedness, including contingency planning, prepositioning of supplies, and surveillance system strengthening.ltbrgtMDM will provide services through supported PHCCs, following WHO and NES Essential Health Package guidelines. These include consultations for communicable and non-communicable diseases, antenatal/postnatal care, skilled birth attendance, and family planning. MHPSS services will be implemented through psychologist case managers and mhGAP-trained doctors, using evidence-based interventions and (like CBT, PM+, mhGAP, PFA) with regular clinical supervision. Integrated care pathways will be supported by staff training in both pharmacological and psychosocial approaches and strong referral systems linking to other sectors, including education, protection, and livelihoods, while emergency referrals will connect patients to higher levels of medical care. ltbrgtCommunity outreach led by CHWs will use IEC materials, group sessions, and radio broadcasts in local languages to raise awareness on MHPSS, SRH, and stigma reduction, supporting positive behaviour change and improve service delivery uptake. To ensure quality and safety, MDM will implement robust IPC protocols, with focal points at each PHCC, regular assessments, and training on hygiene and waste management. Essential medicines and PPE will be procured in line with WHO standards, supported by rational drug use monitoring systems, diversified procurement, and buffer stock strategies to prevent shortages.ltbrgtDisease surveillance and emergency response will be reinforced through EWARS strengthening, rapid response SOPs, staff training, and community engagement strategies. Vulnerable groups, including women, girls, persons with disabilities, and the elderly will be prioritized in both risk communication and service delivery. Sustainable practices will be promoted through improved medical waste management and climate-sensitive training.ltbrgtBuilding on MDM’s health and WASH integration, Acted will provide targeted technical support in health waste management and water quality monitoring, areas where it has proven expertise. This includes advising on WASH intervention design and oversight, adapted to NES operational challenges and global standards. Beyond WASH, Acted’s multisectoral presence adds further value. A coordinated cross-referral system will be established between the two partners: PHCC case managers will refer GBV survivors, persons with disabilities, or those in need of livelihoods assistance to Acted services, while Acted field teams will refer health cases to MDM-supported facilities beyond the scope of the project. This cross-referral mechanism enhances holistic service delivery and reflects a well-coordinated, integrated approach.ltbrgtlt/pgt
